narrative.overview:
Plexus is a calm blue operating layer where cross-border business intent becomes a human-reviewed path to a real meeting and accountable follow-up. Its public world is editorial and assured: saturated blue fields, a midnight logo bay, mineral paper, photographed working context, unified product-system imagery, and tangible agenda fragments explain the journey before they ask for action. The exact Plexus mark remains the identity anchor; it is never redrawn, recolored, or replaced by an improvised symbol.

Authenticated workspaces translate that agenda into an operating system. The typography becomes compact, the canvas shifts to pale mineral blue, and information is grouped with flat cards, hairlines, explicit statuses, and a midnight navigation rail. Connection Blue, cyan, imagery, and motion provide orientation, while product claims, provider readiness, sensitive decisions, and outcomes stay visibly human-governed and evidence-bound.

Authentication is a scoped Governed Checkpoint: a fixed Midnight identity rail uses the approved network field and quiet twinkling nodes before opening into a bright numbered canvas for Identity, Workspace, and Responsible next step. The unboxed credential form occupies the active first lane while later lanes stay visible and ordered. The public pre-event service is a second scoped expression: it uses the shared Midnight, Filled Surface Blue, Connection Blue, cyan, mineral, and pale-network palette with tighter campaign geometry and denser service content.
keyCharacteristics: Saturated production-blue fields anchored by midnight and mineral paper.
Editorial public scale translated into compact operational hierarchy.
Pale network grouping and cyan signals that clarify a governed journey.
Flat, scan-first workspaces with explicit status and human review.
A supplied Midnight network identity rail with reduced-motion-aware twinkling paired with a bright three-stage authentication canvas that becomes one aligned mobile stack.
Pre-launch and capability-readiness qualification placed beside the visual evidence.
The exact Plexus mark, Inter typography, and restrained Geist Mono metadata.
Responsive stacking, mobile navigation sheets, and reduced-motion parity.

rules.name: The Filled Surface Rule
rules.body: Small-text filled actions and active navigation use Filled Surface Blue (`#0758c8`), never the brighter Connection Blue.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Connection Blue and the two cyan values indicate focus, progress, network activity, or ambient energy; they do not independently mean approved, compliant, ready, or successful.

rules.name: The Campaign Cohesion Rule
rules.body: The pre-event route uses the shared blue palette while retaining its compact 4px controls and service-led density. Signal Cyan may orient visitors on Midnight, but Filled Surface Blue remains the small-text action color.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries the main Plexus voice across public, authenticated, and localized surfaces; do not introduce a decorative display face.

rules.name: The Metadata Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking and Geist Mono are reserved for short orientation or technical metadata; they are not the default preheading treatment for every section.

rules.name: The Sheet-not-Squeeze Rule
rules.body: Mobile navigation opens as a left sheet; never compress the desktop rail into an unreadable strip.

rules.name: The Record-not-Scroll Rule
rules.body: Dense operational tables become stacked record cards on narrow screens instead of depending on horizontal page scrolling.

rules.name: The Preview First-Viewport Rule
rules.body: On mobile product previews, keep the promise, full-width primary action, pre-launch qualification, and unified product image in that order before the journey rail; do not lead with a detached feature card or hide qualification below the first product view.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If surface tone, spacing, and a hairline already establish hierarchy, do not add a shadow.

rules.name: The Governed Checkpoint Rule
rules.body: Authentication depth comes from the hard transition between the fixed Midnight identity rail and bright ordered stage canvas; backdrop blur and translucent glass are reserved for temporary overlays.

rules.name: The Curve by Scale Rule
rules.body: Controls are tighter than cards, cards are tighter than editorial frames, and authentication follows the same hierarchy instead of introducing an oversized glass radius.

rules.name: The Same State Rule
rules.body: Desktop rail, mobile sheet, table card, dialog, and localized variant must expose the same route, status, and next action.

rules.name: The Human-Governed Rule
rules.body: Components may assist matching, preparation, and follow-up, but visual polish never turns a planned adapter, sensitive decision, or unverified outcome into a production claim.

rules.name: The Qualification-at-the-Point Rule
rules.body: Every illustrative product treatment carries its qualification beside the visual or module copy, and every readiness label appears with the shared legend; a page-level disclaimer alone is insufficient.

dos: Do use Filled Surface Blue (`#0758c8`) for compact filled actions and active destinations.
Do keep Connection Blue (`#0a84ff`) for focus, progress, selection, large ambient fields, and other high-visibility signals.
Do pair every status color with readable text or an icon and preserve explicit human review.
Do preserve the exact Plexus wordmark asset and approved tenant identity without weakening contrast.
Do use mineral canvases, Pale Network grouping, and hairlines before reaching for elevation.
Do verify mobile sheet navigation, stacked records, longer translated labels, keyboard focus, and reduced motion.

Do keep authentication's Governed Checkpoint ordered across the identity rail, three-stage header, credentials, and support, and preserve the pre-event route's compact campaign geometry within the shared blue palette.
Do place pre-launch, illustrative, and readiness qualification beside the relevant product image or module copy.
Do preserve the capability bento's unequal editorial proportions, attached readiness chips, and one-column narrow-mobile reading order.
donts: Don't use Connection Blue as the filled background behind small white CTA text.
Don't revive Harbor Teal, emerald, or lime as competing campaign accents inside the shared blue editorial system.
Don't float every operational card or apply glass and glow to routine workspace content.
Don't compress desktop rails or dense tables into unreadable mobile layouts.
Don't redraw, recolor, crop into a new symbol, or substitute the Plexus mark.
Don't use animation, color, badges, or polished imagery as evidence of approval, compliance, provider readiness, market coverage, or business outcomes.
Don't reuse Live, Mixed, Adapter, and Concept colors as generic success, warning, or category styling.
Don't generalize the capability bento's cream cards or unequal proportions into a new global card system; its PLEXA route reuses the established Filled Surface Blue action role.
